passages.title: The Rise of Repairable Electronics
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of technology, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Components fixed with strong adhesive can be difficult to remove without damage. Modular products allow a faulty component to be replaced without discarding the whole device.
A device may become less useful when software updates stop. Detailed repair manuals help technicians identify and fix faults.
The price of replacement parts can determine whether repair is worthwhile. Independent repair services depend on being able to obtain suitable components.
Some designs that improve water resistance also make devices harder to open. Demand for repairable products may influence manufacturers' design choices.

passages.title: Measuring Happiness in Cities
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of social science, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Income is one factor, but it does not describe every aspect of wellbeing. Relationships and social support can affect how people evaluate their lives.
The wording of a survey question can influence the answers people give. An average score can conceal substantial differences between groups.
Access to parks and natural areas is one factor researchers examine. Repeated measurements can show how wellbeing changes over time.
Cultural differences can influence how people interpret wellbeing questions. Decision-makers should consider multiple forms of evidence rather than one measure alone.

passages.title: The History of Weather Forecasting
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of science, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Early forecasts were based largely on observations of local weather patterns. Telegraph networks allowed weather observations to be shared more quickly.
Weather satellites observe large areas of the atmosphere and Earth's surface. Numerical models calculate how atmospheric conditions may evolve.
Forecasts tend to become less certain further into the future. Mountains, valleys and coastlines can affect local weather.
Ensemble forecasting compares several model runs to estimate uncertainty. Clear warnings help people understand forecast risks and decide how to respond.
